emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(timer->state)]) from thread_b (the lockless hrtimer_is_queued read must not race a concurrent state write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: the writer holds the per-CPU timer base lock, but hrtimer_is_queued reads timer->state intentionally lockless from softirq/IRQ vs task context; the two accesses share no lock, so no serialize(g) establishes the single-access atomicity the reader assumes
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write to the one-byte state field -> data race (KCSAN reported)

fix_maps_to: patch wraps the writes (enqueue_hrtimer/__remove_hrtimer) in WRITE_ONCE and the read (hrtimer_is_queued) in READ_ONCE -> makes the conflicting single access atomic; this is a tearing annotation, not a serialize/order/counts synchronization guarantee
recall_risk_notes: Object and sites are in the static surface, so the pair is findable, and the category maps to atomic(single access)=data_race. But hrtimer_is_queued is explicitly documented as a lockless snapshot that tolerates staleness, so the reader carries no semantic order intent beyond no-tearing. Our design wants an order/atomicity intent; here the LLM is likely to adjudicate the read as a benign best-effort snapshot and reject it (precision pressure), or only a pure-syntactic-race detector would flag it. The added READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE does not map onto serialize/order/counts.
